The Sub-Inspector of Police of J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru City has filed Police Report against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. It is the case of the Prosecution that the Inspector of Department of Legal Metrology had information that this accused without being qualified as a B.Sc. Or Diploma in Electricals or Electronics or with any other qualification was repairing the electronic items by taking huge amount from the customers.
This accused even had taken an amount of Rs.4,720/- from one of the customers and caused loss to the Department.

Based on the information, CW1 had been to the Srinivas Chicken Centre wherein this accused was repairing the electronic items without of qualification and without any valid license and permit for his illegal gains.
CW1 had seized the receipt issued by the accused to an amount of Rs.4,720/- to one of the customers by conducting the seizure panchanama.
CW1 has lodged the information.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.236/2021 at J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru City.
During investigation, the accused has appeared before the Court and enlarged on bail.

On completion of the investigation, the Sub-Inspector of Police of J.P.Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru filed Police Report against the accused alleging that he has committed the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
After taking cognizance of the said offence, the process was issued to the accused.
The copies of the Police Report and other Prosecution papers are furnished to the accused under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the the accused has committed the offence triable by this Court, charges for the offence have been framed and read over to him in Kannada language.
He has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
4. To prove the charges framed against the accused, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidences of PW1 to PW3 and the documentary evidences in Ex.P1 to Ex.P6.

After completion of the Prosecution evidences, for the purpose of enabling the accused personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution against him, examined the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
He has submitted that he has no defense evidence.
5. Heard the arguments of learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor.
Perused the materials available on record.

6. The points for determination are;
1. Whether prosecution has proved the offence charged against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubts?
2. What order or sentence?
7.

My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,

sentences.text: 9. To prove the guilt of the accused the Prosecution has examined CW1/PW1 Smt.Bhavya, Inspector of Legal Metrology wherein this witness has deposed that on 27.11.2021 she was informed that this accused without any valid license and permit repairing the electronic items.
This accused even had issued the receipt for repair of one electronic item for Rs.4,720/-.
The accused had repaired four weighing machines of one of the customers.
This accused has caused loss to the Department and accordingly she has lodged the information against this accused.
10. The Prosecution has examined CW2/PW2 Ramesh wherein this has deposed that this accused had taken an amount of Rs.4720/- for repairing his scale machines.
This accused even has issued Receipt for the amount of Rs.4,720/-.
11. The Prosecution has examined CW3/PW3 Karagaiah who is an Investigation Officer has deposed about that investigation conducted by him at the time of filing of the Final Report.
12. It is the case of the Prosecution that this accused without valid license, permit and also without any qualification was repairing the electronic items.
The accused even had taken an amount of Rs.4720/- for repairing the weighing machine of one Mr.Ramesh, CW2.

13. CW1 has lodged the information and in her information herself has stated that she came to know that this accused had taken her photos during the time of execution of her official work and trying to spoil her reputation.
CW1 in her evidence has deposed totally inconsistent to her own information.
She has deposed that this accused has repaired four weighing machine of one Mr.Ramesh.
This accused has even issued one Receipt for the repair of the said machine.
This informant has produced the Receipt for the payment of the said electronic machine as per Ex.P3 has not at all mentioned that the said Receipt is for the repair of weighing machine.
In her cross-examination she has further deposed that this accused has lodged complaint against her.
The official has been conducting DE-Enquiry against her.
Further, in her cross-examination she has admitted that she has already filed private complaint against this accused during the year 2022.
As per legal metrology Act, she has to file private complaint against this accused.
But however, she has lodged the information against this accused which is contrary to the said legal Act.
As per the information, this accused has repaired one weighing machine belongs to one Mr.Ramesh.
But however in her evidence she has deposed that this accused has repaired four weighing machines.
Further, the witness has deposed that she has conducted the seizure panchanama and seized the Receipts for the repair of said weighing machines.
But however she has not produced the said weighing machines before this Court, nor she has taken the photos of the machines.
To prove the seizure, CW1 has produced only the Bill alleged to be issued by this accused as per Ex.P4 which contains the name of the Enterprise as Anugraha Enterprise.
On perusal of the said Ex.P4, Tax Invoice Receipts, it also contains the License Number and the permission obtained from the Legal Metrology.

sentences.text: It is not the case of the informant that this Ex.P4 is created by this accused or they have not issued any license to run the shop for repairing the electronic instruments.
The informant further has alleged that she has even lodged the complaint under Sections 200 for the violation of Section 23 of the Legal Metrology Act.
But however, how the information filed before the SHO and how this complaint is maintainable against this accused?
CW1 herself in her evidence has deposed that this accused has lodged many complaints against the informant and the Domestic Enquiry is progress.
It looks that to overcome or to take retaliation the informant has filed this false case against this accused.
Further, even the informant has not produced any document to show the existence of the said shop in his name.
CW2/PW2 who is one Mr.Ramesh and whose weighing machine was alleged to be repaired by this accused has deposed that he is having a chicken Center and he is selling chickens of 100 to 150 kgs per day.
But however, to weigh such kgs of chickens, four to five weighing machines are not required.
This witness has not at all deposed that his four weighing machines were repaired by this accused.
This witness even has not at all identified this accused before this Court and has denied that this accused has repaired his weighing machines.
As said supra, the informant has lodged the information on grudge against this accused for the complaint lodged against this accused.
without any evidence and without any documents the information was lodged and the Investigation Officer without applying his mind has filed the Final Report against this accused.
at least the informant has to seize the weighing machines or to produced the documents to show that this accused owns such kind of shops in his name.
It looks that the Receipt produced before this Court contains the name of Anugrapha Enterprises.
In a proprietary column the name of Manju is written.
But, it looks very unusal to write a name in the Proprietor column.
It is nothing but, this document is created to file a false case against this accused.
the offence alleged against this accused is under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
but, how the accused has played fraud of cheated the Department is a riddle before the Court.
The alleged Receipt obtained by this accused containes the permission taken by him from the Department and it also containes the Licence Number.
Neither the informant nor the Investigation Officer has collected any document to show the license and the permit obtained by this accused.
The Prosecution even after lapse of six years is able to examine only three witnesses out of five.
Absolutely there is no evidence available before the court to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

15. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the accused is not found guilty for the aforesaid offence charged against him.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDERS Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C, the accused is hereby acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.
His bail bond and surety bond executed will be in force till appeal period and thereafter, it shall stand canceled.
